title: Data-driven prediction of polymer surface adhesion using high-throughput MD and hybrid network models
experiments_summary: 1) Polymer and surface generation: Coarse-grained polymer sequences (40-bead chains) and surface patterns (20×20 lattices) were generated using 1D and 2D Ising Monte Carlo simulations with the Metropolis-Hastings algorithm, incorporating a biasing term for fraction control. Compositions of strongly (A/A') and weakly (B/B') interacting beads were varied from 0.1 to 0.9 in steps of 0.1, with 10 independent configurations sampled per fraction, yielding 92 unique surface patterns and 92 unique polymer sequences. Surfaces used a hexagonal closed-packing lattice with adsorption energies ranging from 10 to 70 k_BT across four fixed layers. 2) Molecular dynamics simulations: All MD simulations were conducted using GROMACS 2021.4. Polymer bonded interactions used the FENE potential; a flat-bottom potential confined the polymer laterally. A Langevin thermostat maintained temperature at 300 K. Simulations ran for 4,000,000 steps (20 ns). Surface beads were fixed; polymers moved freely in three dimensions. 3) Umbrella sampling: Free energy profiles (PMFs) were computed via umbrella sampling using the polymer center-of-mass distance from the surface along the z-axis as the collective variable. A harmonic bias potential with force constant 500 kJ mol⁻¹ nm⁻² was applied across 58 windows spanning CV values from 0 to 10 nm. PMF profiles were reconstructed and binding free energies (ΔF) were extracted. 4) Data preprocessing and augmentation: Symmetry-based canonical-form reduction was applied to surfaces (90°, 180°, 270° rotations and horizontal/vertical flips) and polymer sequences (reversal) to eliminate redundant configurations. Each surface was represented as a binary 20×20 one-hot-encoded matrix; each polymer as a binary 40-element sequence. 5) Hybrid deep learning model construction: A hybrid CNN-GRU-Transformer model was built to predict full PMF profiles from surface-polymer pairs. The surface branch reshaped input to a 20×20×1 tensor processed through three 2D convolutional layers with increasing filter depths and max-pooling, followed by a dense layer projecting to a 64-dimensional feature vector. The polymer branch reshaped input to (40,1) and processed it through a single-layer GRU. A cross-attention transformer block was applied with GRU output as query and CNN surface encoding as keys and values, using multi-head attention followed by a feed-forward network and residual connections. The combined output was flattened and passed through a feed-forward network to predict the 100-point PMF profile. Full architecture hyperparameters are reported in Table S1. 6) Model evaluation and ablation: The hybrid model was benchmarked against a baseline deep neural network (DNN) using the same input representations. An ablation study on the polymer encoder was conducted, comparing 1D CNN, GRU, BiGRU, LSTM, and BiLSTM alternatives while keeping the 2D CNN surface encoder fixed. Attention outputs were projected into two dimensions using t-SNE for interpretability analysis.
